sections.hypothesis: Coins that follow BTC (ETH, SOL) trend in weekly steps: holding one for the week after its Sunday-to-Sunday return was positive, and cash after a negative week, beats holding it on risk-adjusted return, after costs. BTC itself is not part of the claim.
sections.rationale: Formed from results, and said so: the one-week-momentum note (rejected 2026-11-13) passed every rule on ETH 2020-25 (Sharpe 1.23 vs 1.12, drawdown -42% vs -79%, better Sharpe than holding from 83% of 2-year start dates) but failed on BTC (Sharpe 0.94 vs 1.07, better from only 34% of starts). An idea formed from data is only evidence when tested on data that played no part in forming it, so this note tests it on ETH's earlier years and on a coin never run with it. Proposed mechanism (Luke's): BTC leads and the large alts follow with a lag, so their weekly moves continue more than BTC's do. If that is the mechanism, BTC's own weekly return should also predict ETH and SOL; that is a different strategy and a separate trial, noted here as a follow-up, not tested. Weak points: the ETH window is short (about 2.4 years, roughly 125 weekly decisions); SOL is tested over the same 2020-25 years the idea came from, and SOL and ETH are highly correlated, so SOL is a new market but not new time; and after about 150 trials, a pass is still modest evidence. Liu and Tsyvinski (NBER w24877) report weekly time-series momentum in crypto generally.
sections.rules: Implementation weekly-momentum, unchanged. Daily bars. At each Sunday's close (UTC), the week's return is the close over the close exactly 7 days earlier (looked up by date; a missing start bar means no signal, cash). Positive: target weight 1 until the next Sunday's close; otherwise 0. Decide at the close, trade at the next open; 2% no-trade band; long only, spot; 10 bps fee, 1 bp half-spread, square-root impact.
sections.falsification: Two runs, once each, 330 USDT: ETHUSDT 1d 2017-08 to 2019-12 (unseen by this strategy: every earlier weekly-momentum run started 2020-01) and SOLUSDT 1d 2020-08 to 2025-10 (SOL's whole research history, never run with this strategy). Reject unless, on both: (1) Sharpe above buy-and-hold's; (2) total return beats the coin held at the strategy's average exposure; (3) max drawdown smaller than buy-and-hold's; (4) break-even cost at least twice the cost paid; (5) better Sharpe than holding from at least 60% of 1-year start dates (the run's start-date table). Changed from the earlier note, decided before any run: 'P(profit) at least 90%' is replaced by rule 3, because the ETH window contains the 2018 crash (ETH fell about 90% from its peak) and a strategy can be clearly better than holding there without making money; rule 5 is new, from the start-date comparison built 2026-11-13. A pass moves it to Watch, not Pursue; the holdout (from 2025-11) stays untouched.
sections.parameters: None: the one-week horizon is the hypothesis.
sections.costs: About 15-25 round trips a year at about 22 bps each, 3-6% a year. The earlier ETH run paid 23 bps per round trip against a 277 bps break-even.
